scenes.heading: Pythagoras in 3D
scenes.sub: Will the umbrella fit in the suitcase?
scenes.say: Will a long umbrella fit in your suitcase? How tall is a cone-shaped tent? Pythagoras works in three dimensions too. You just need to find the flat right-angled triangle hiding inside the solid.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.everyday: A thin sheet of glass slid diagonally into a shoebox
scenes.science: A flat right-angled triangle hidden inside the solid
scenes.breaks: Real glass has thickness. Our triangles are perfectly flat lines.
scenes.say: Imagine sliding a thin sheet of glass diagonally into a shoebox. On that flat sheet you can draw a right-angled triangle. Every 3D Pythagoras problem is really a 2D problem on a hidden flat sheet.

scenes.heading: Across the floor, then up
scenes.say: Here's a box twelve by four by three centimetres. First draw the dashed diagonal across the floor: twelve squared plus four squared is one hundred and sixty. Then the space diagonal goes up to the opposite corner: one hundred and sixty plus three squared is one hundred and sixty-nine. So d is thirteen centimetres.
scenes.caption: Floor: 12² + 4² = 160. Up: 160 + 3² = 169. d = √169 = 13 cm.

scenes.heading: The space diagonal shortcut
parts: length and width of the base
scenes.say: Both steps together give a shortcut. d squared equals l squared plus w squared plus h squared. Square all three, add, then take the square root.

scenes.heading: The triangle inside a cone
scenes.say: In a cone, the radius, the height and the slant height make a right-angled triangle. With radius six and height nine, s squared is thirty-six plus eighty-one, which is one hundred and seventeen. So the slant height is about ten point eight centimetres.
scenes.caption: s² = 6² + 9² = 36 + 81 = 117, so s ≈ 10.8 cm.

scenes.heading: Longest straw in a can
scenes.question: A can is 7 cm wide and 12 cm tall. Find the longest straw that fits inside.
scenes.say: A can is seven centimetres across and twelve tall. The straw goes across the full diameter and up the height. Seven squared plus twelve squared is one hundred and ninety-three. The square root is about thirteen point nine centimetres.
scenes.caption: 7² + 12² = 49 + 144 = 193. x = √193 ≈ 13.9 cm.

scenes.heading: Watch out for
points: Don’t stop at the floor diagonal
scenes.say: Watch out for these traps. Don't stop at the floor diagonal. Carry b squared into the next step without rounding. In a cylinder, use the diameter. And in a pyramid, halve the base first, because the height lands in the middle.

Recap. Find the flat right-angled triangle inside the solid. For a box, go across the floor then up, or use d squared equals l squared plus w squared plus h squared. For a cone, s squared equals r squared plus h squared. Now try the practice questions!
